title: Nikita P NDE 9899
content: I was at the youth festival concert. I wasn't sure what the point of life was, but I wasn't feeling depressed. In fact, I had a cold. I had just left the stuffy, concert venue. I stood on a balance board and then fell off, hitting the ground. It was painful. I was scared, as the fall had happened unexpectedly and quickly. Then, I felt sick and sat down on the curb. I told my friend that I was about to faint. He didn't believe me and thought I was joking. As I lost consciousness, I fell; hitting my neck and arm. I started seeing rapid hallucinations. My mind seemed to slow down. It was as if two minutes without consciousness felt like five seconds. At first, I heard a mix of chorus sounds that came from far away. It seemed that the voice of the choir was in my head, and the music was far away. The sound was far from me. While I was unconscious, I heard it the music quite loudly. I heard several minutes of singing in a couple of seconds. I was terrified. Despite being confused, I could understand where I was, and the location of objects around me. I knew where the voices were coming from, and knew that the people were behind a venue wall. I could still hear choir voices inside my head. Then, I saw darkness and began to realize that I might be dying. I saw a strange sphere that looked like a glass ball or an optical distortion; similar to an ultra-wide-angle fish-eye lens. There were objects inside the sphere. Or rather, there were moments from the current reality. They looked like spots, inside which there were images of the surroundings around me. These included lantern garlands, spruce, a man with a festival merch hood, whose face I could not see. There was also a road with puddles, and several other objects that I didn't have time to examine. I could see these images and instantly approached. It was as if I saw flashes of moments from reality. It is difficult to describe exactly how this happened, since I moved away and approached each image if I wanted to examine it further. I didn't physically moved to the objects, just overviewed them. While I was moving away from and approaching each image, I figured out it was an environment surrounding me. I realized that I hadn't achieved everything I wanted yet on this earth. So, I made a choice to return to my current reality. After coming back, I felt shaken and afraid of fainting again. The nurse had me inhale some ammonia and I started to feel a little better. I continued to shake. It was late, and I went to the camp building to sleep. After returning, I started to think more and more that our world may not be real. I thought that it could be just one of many worlds, or that we could be living in a simulation. I have not been able to discover what lies on the other side. After this experience, I realized that death is not something to be afraid of. Background Information: Gender: Male Date NDE Occurred: 06.09.2023 NDE Elements: At the time of your experience, was there an associated life-threatening event? No. Spinal cord concussion from falling to the ground due to fainting. Illness, trauma or other condition not considered life threatening. I fell, fainted, and hit the ground with my neck How do you consider the content of your experience? Entirely distressing Did you feel separated from your body? No I lost awareness of my body How did your highest level of consciousness and alertness during the experience compare to your normal everyday consciousness and alertness? Normal consciousness and alertness. My level of alertness was as normal as usual At what time during the experience were you at your highest level of consciousness and alertness? I saw a sphere Were your thoughts speeded up? No Did time seem to speed up or slow down? Time seemed to go faster or slower than usual. My consciousness slowed down; 5 seconds in my experience was 2 minutes in reality Were your senses More vivid than usual? More vivid than usual Please compare your vision during the experience to your everyday vision that you had immediately prior to the time of the experience. My vision was different from what I see in regular life. A little misty, but photo-realistic. Close to the real life vision Please compare your hearing during the experience to your everyday hearing that you had immediately prior to the time of the experience. My hearing was better than usual, but sounds I listened to were fast Did you seem to be aware of things going on elsewhere? No Did you pass into or through a tunnel? No Did you see any beings in your experience? No Did you encounter or become aware of any deceased (or alive) beings? No Did you see, or feel surrounded by, a brilliant light? No Did you see an unearthly light? No Did you seem to enter some other, unearthly world? No What emotions did you feel during the experience? I was scared and anxious Did you have a feeling of peace or pleasantness? No Did you have a feeling of joy? No Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity with the universe? No Did you suddenly seem to understand everything? No Did scenes from your past come back to you? No Did scenes from the future come to you? No Did you come to a border or point of no return? I came to a definite conscious decision to return to life. I was scared and wanted to live. I made a choice to live as it was an option. The other option was to not to return God, Spiritual and Religion: What was your religion prior to your experience? Unaffiliated- Atheist Have your religious practices changed since your experience? No What is your religion now? Unaffiliated- Agnostic Did your experience include features consistent with your earthly beliefs? Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience. Before the experience I wasn't sure if there are multiple worlds or how our universe was born. At the time of my experience, I understood that returning back to life is a personal choice Did you have a change in your values and beliefs because of your experience? Yes I started to believe that our life is simulation or game in which gamers play as some of persons. The simulation is adaptable, but not perfect. It learns how to seem to be as real as possible and defends the laws. People who believe they can control the circumstances can do so, but only if that doesn't interrupt intentions of other players. Did you seem to encounter a mystical being or presence, or hear an unidentifiable voice? No Did you see deceased or religious spirits? No Did you encounter or become aware of any beings who previously lived on earth who are described by name in religions (for example: Jesus, Muhammad, Buddha, etc.)? No During your experience, did you gain information about premortal existence? No During your experience, did you gain information about universal connection or oneness? No During your experience, did you gain information about the existence of God? No Concerning our Earthly lives other than Religion: During your experience, did you gain special knowledge or information about your purpose? No During your experience, did you gain information about the meaning of life? No During your experience, did you gain information about an afterlife? No Did you gain information about how to live our lives? No During your experience, did you gain information about life's difficulties, challenges and hardships? No During your experience, did you gain information about love? No What life changes occurred in your life after your experience? Slight changes in my life. I began to perceive life as a game in which you have an advantage over other players in something that others do not have After the NDE: Was the experience difficult to express in words? No How accurately do you remember the experience in comparison to other life events that occurred around the time of the experience? I remember the experience as accurately as other life events that occurred around the time of the experience. I remember my experience as accurate as I experienced other events that occurred with me at that time Do you have any psychic, non-ordinary or other special gifts after your experience that you did not have before the experience? Uncertain With the focused intentions, I can control circumstances in my life. Not sure how it works, still in researching and testing this skill to prove that it's real and controllable Are there one or several parts of your experience that are especially meaningful or significant to you? The second part with sphere Have you ever shared this experience with others? Yes I shared my full experience in a week or two Did you have any knowledge of near death experience (NDE) prior to your experience? Uncertain First time I knew about NDE was the Netflix show 'The OA'. I had superficial knowledge about NDE. It doesn't affected my NDE, my experience was unique in its own way. What did you believe about the reality of your experience shortly (days to weeks) after it happened? Experience was probably real. I felt real fear and was conscious during the experience. I controlled my decisions What do you believe about the reality of your experience now? Experience was definitely real. I felt real fear and was conscious during the experience. I controlled my decisions. I still remember it, but my sleep dreams are fading within time At any time in your life, has anything ever reproduced any part of the experience? No i36w2n5_nde

elements.i36w2n5_nde: Description I was at the youth festival concert. I wasn't sure what the point of life was, but I wasn't feeling depressed. In fact, I had a cold. I had just left the stuffy, concert venue. I stood on a balance board and then fell off, hitting the ground. It was painful. I was scared, as the fall had happened unexpectedly and quickly. Then, I felt sick and sat down on the curb. I told my friend that I was about to faint. He didn't believe me and thought I was joking. As I lost consciousness, I fell; hitting my neck and arm. I started seeing rapid hallucinations. My mind seemed to slow down. It was as if two minutes without consciousness felt like five seconds. At first, I heard a mix of chorus sounds that came from far away. It seemed that the voice of the choir was in my head, and the music was far away. The sound was far from me. While I was unconscious, I heard it the music quite loudly. I heard several minutes of singing in a couple of seconds. I was terrified. Despite being confused, I could understand where I was, and the location of objects around me. I knew where the voices were coming from, and knew that the people were behind a venue wall. I could still hear choir voices inside my head. Then, I saw darkness and began to realize that I might be dying. I saw a strange sphere that looked like a glass ball or an optical distortion; similar to an ultra-wide-angle fish-eye lens. There were objects inside the sphere. Or rather, there were moments from the current reality. They looked like spots, inside which there were images of the surroundings around me. These included lantern garlands, spruce, a man with a festival merch hood, whose face I could not see. There was also a road with puddles, and several other objects that I didn't have time to examine. I could see these images and instantly approached. It was as if I saw flashes of moments from reality. It is difficult to describe exactly how this happened, since I moved away and approached each image if I wanted to examine it further. I didn't physically moved to the objects, just overviewed them. While I was moving away from and approaching each image, I figured out it was an environment surrounding me. I realized that I hadn't achieved everything I wanted yet on this earth. So, I made a choice to return to my current reality. After coming back, I felt shaken and afraid of fainting again. The nurse had me inhale some ammonia and I started to feel a little better. I continued to shake. It was late, and I went to the camp building to sleep. After returning, I started to think more and more that our world may not be real. I thought that it could be just one of many worlds, or that we could be living in a simulation. I have not been able to discover what lies on the other side. After this experience, I realized that death is not something to be afraid of.
